summary: Over 11 days in October the customer made 6 branch cash deposits, every one just under GBP 10,000. Across all recorded history, 51 deposits have stayed in the same band and none reached GBP 10,000. The customer is a declared cash-intensive market business whose declared income broadly matches the cash volumes, most of the money stayed in the account and outgoing payments look routine. However, no business records or source-of-funds documents are on file, and the account shows none of the operating costs a trading business would normally have.

evidence.claim: 6 branch cash deposits between 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-17, one every 2 days, GBP 8,190.49 to 9,891.42 each, total GBP 55,175.26, all below GBP 10,000.

Branch cash is the only source of money in across recorded history: 51 deposits totalling GBP 463,173.10 from 2026-05-01 to 2026-10-17, averaging about GBP 9,082. No cash deposit of GBP 10,000 or more was found in either window.

The pattern is not new. The earlier window had 9 cash deposits from 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-25 (GBP 8,022.07 to 9,939.00, total GBP 83,270.65), 5 of them within 13 days. The alert window differs mainly in spacing: every 2 days instead of every 3.
Funds were not moved on: GBP 55,175.26 came in and GBP 2,510.57 went out in the alert window, so about 95% stayed in the account.

Outflows are routine and match the baseline: the same 3 monthly direct debits (GBP 570.00, 798.00, 1,026.00) on the same days of the month, plus small card payments of GBP 5.00 to 11.29. Baseline outflows were GBP 2,514.44 against GBP 2,510.57 in the alert window.
All counterparties are in GB and at the same bank, and none pays money in apart from the cash branch. There were no sanctions, PEP or adverse media matches for the customer.

KYC records a cash market business with declared income of GBP 927,000. About GBP 463k over about 5.5 months annualises to roughly GBP 1.0m, which broadly fits. The customer risk rating is Low even though the business is cash-intensive.
No cash deposits were made after 2026-10-17. Only small card payments followed, up to 2026-10-28.

innocent_explanations: A declared market trader banking takings every 2 to 3 days could produce regular deposits of similar size, and busier trading in early October could explain the tighter spacing.
The business may bank each trading day's or market's takings as one deposit, and these may tend to fall between GBP 8k and 10k.
Declared income of GBP 927,000 broadly matches the annualised cash volume, and outgoing payments are steady and routine.
The gap after 2026-10-17 could reflect a break in trading, such as the end of a season or a holiday.
gaps: No business records, takings data or source-of-funds/source-of-wealth documents to show the cash is genuine trading income.
Unexplained why none of 51 deposits reached GBP 10,000, when real takings would usually vary more.

The account shows none of the outflows a trading business would normally have (suppliers, stock, wages, rent, pitch fees). Unknown whether the business banks elsewhere. Outflows were only measured in the two windows.
No transaction history before 2026-05-01 even though the account opened 2022-12-26. Unclear whether the pattern started in May 2026 or the data is missing.
Nothing on file explains the Low risk rating for a cash-intensive business.
Unknown why cash deposits stopped after 2026-10-17.
